body.statement: For each \(a\in\{1,2\}\), every \(q\)-state triangular view satisfying the Markov factorization obeys \(\det(M_a)=\varepsilon_{q,K}\prod_{k=1}^K\prod_{u\in\mathcal Q^{k-1}}\det(B_{a,k,u})^{q^{K-k}}=\varepsilon_{q,K}\Delta_a\).
body.justification: The factorization exposes every load-bearing categorical contrast rather than hiding failure in a global generic-rank condition.
body.gap: Lee and Gu (2026, Appendix D and Appendix G) prove a binary recursion and display a ternary obstruction, but do not give the all-\(q\), all-context product.
body.consumer: It gives a finite symbolic certificate for proposed polytomous cognitive-diagnosis tables.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(a\in\{1,2\}\), suppress \(a\) from the notation, and relabel the latent coordinates in the order \(\rho_a\). Write \(X_k=X_{s(a,k)}\) and \(H_{1:k}=(H_{\rho_a(1)},\ldots,H_{\rho_a(k)})\). By Assumption~\textnormal{ass:double-triangular}, every latent parent of \(X_k\) is among \(H_{1:k}\), and \(H_k\) is a parent. Assumption~\textnormal{ass:markov} therefore gives
\[
 P(X_{1:m}=x_{1:m}\mid H=h)
 =\prod_{k=1}^{m}P(X_k=x_k\mid H_{1:k}=h_{1:k})
 =\prod_{k=1}^{m}B_{a,k,h_{1:k-1}}(x_k,h_k).
\]
The first equality uses conditional independence of the observed vertices given all latent vertices; the second uses the absence of later latent parents. In particular, the expression does not depend on \(h_{m+1:K}\).

Let \(M^{(m)}\) be the \(q^m\times q^m\) matrix with the displayed product as its \((x_{1:m},h_{1:m})\) entry. With rows and columns in the induced lexicographic orders, insertion of the intermediate index \((h_{1:m-1},y_m)\) gives, up to the fixed row and column permutations used by the stated conventions,
\[
 M^{(m)}=(M^{(m-1)}\otimes I_q)
 \operatorname{blockdiag}_{u\in\mathcal Q^{m-1}}B_{a,m,u}.
\]
Indeed, the \((x_{1:m},h_{1:m})\) entry of the right-hand side is
\[
 \sum_{u,y_m}M^{(m-1)}(x_{1:m-1},u)
 \mathbf 1\{x_m=y_m\}\mathbf 1\{u=h_{1:m-1}\}
 B_{a,m,u}(y_m,h_m),
\]
which is exactly the preceding product formula. Multiplicativity of the determinant, the block-diagonal determinant formula, and \(\det(C\otimes I_q)=\det(C)^q\) now yield
\[
 \det M^{(m)}=\epsilon_m\det(M^{(m-1)})^q
 \prod_{u\in\mathcal Q^{m-1}}\det(B_{a,m,u}),
\]
where \(\epsilon_m\in\{-1,1\}\) records only the fixed permutations. Starting with \(M^{(1)}=B_{a,1,\varnothing}\) and iterating from \(m=2\) to \(m=K\), a determinant introduced at level \(k\) is raised to the \(q\)-th power once for every later level. Hence
\[
 \det(M_a)=\varepsilon_{q,K}
 \prod_{k=1}^{K}\prod_{u\in\mathcal Q^{k-1}}
 \det(B_{a,k,u})^{q^{K-k}}
 =\varepsilon_{q,K}\Delta_a.
\]
All matrices are finite and square, and no division or limiting argument is used.
